# connect

Open a connection to a server

## Synopsis

```
cdb connect [profile | url] [flags]
```

## Description

Open a connection to a server.

A server URL with no user name and password is asked about: a CouchDB with an admin
accepts an anonymous connection and then refuses every command, so connect asks for
credentials first. Pass --anonymous to connect without any, or set CDB_USER and
CDB_PASSWORD.

## Arguments

Takes at most 1 argument.

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--as` | string |  | profile name to save under |
| `--save` | bool | `false` | save the connection as a profile after connecting |

## Global flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--anonymous` | bool | `false` | connect without credentials, and do not ask for any |
| `--color` | string |  | colour: auto, always or never |
| `--format` | string |  | output format: table or json |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | print raw JSON instead of a table |
| `--pager` | string |  | pager command, or off |
| `--path` | string |  | starting virtual path |
| `--profile` | string |  | connection profile to use, overriding CDB_PROFILE and the default |
| `--url` | string |  | server URL, overriding the profile and CDB_URL |
| `--verbose` | bool | `false` | include raw status codes and reasons in errors |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | skip confirmation prompts |

## Examples

```
$ cdb connect --save --as local http://admin:password@localhost:5984/
Connected to CouchDB 3.5.2 at localhost:5984 as admin.

$ cdb connect local
Connected to CouchDB 3.5.2 at localhost:5984 as admin.
```
